intro: The Chargers fell to 0-6, and the Rams lost Davante Adams and their kicker in a last-second loss at Arizona. Brock Purdy's career passer rating now tops the NFL's all-time list as the 49ers reach 6-0, and the unbeaten Chiefs visit Seattle on Sunday night. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Chargers fall to 0-6 as Harbaugh promises an offensive review
top.dek: Kansas City won 22-6 and sent Los Angeles into its bye winless. The Chargers reached the Chiefs' 1-yard line before a holding penalty cut the drive to a field goal. Jim Harbaugh said the offense is not scoring enough and he will look at everything.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Rams lose Davante Adams for 6 to 10 weeks, plus kicker Blake Grupe
top.dek: Adams ruptured a hamstring tendon, and Grupe (torn ACL) and nose tackle Poona Ford (ruptured triceps) are done for the season. Kobie Turner has a groin strain and likely heads to IR. Trent McDuffie's groin status for Las Vegas gets decided at the end of the week.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Chad Ryland kicks six field goals, the last one on the final snap
top.dek: Ryland accounted for all 18 Arizona points, and his 43-yarder as time expired beat the Rams 18-16. Jacoby Brissett added 218 passing yards. The loss dropped Los Angeles to 2-4.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 105.6: Brock Purdy's career passer rating, best in NFL history
top.dek: Purdy passed the 1,500-attempt mark, which puts his rating above Lamar Jackson's 102.7 for the top career number. He went 21 of 29 for 264 yards as San Francisco held off Washington to reach 6-0.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs visit the Seahawks on Sunday night
top.dek: Kansas City, 5-0, plays at Lumen Field on Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Seattle is 3-3 after a 17-14 overtime loss in Denver. Thursday night opens the week with the Patriots at the Bears.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit the bye at 5-1 after a 33-30 escape

stories.text: Bills survive Las Vegas and head into the bye at 5-1
stories.summary: Buffalo beat the Raiders 33-30 on the road after leading 23-13 through three quarters. Las Vegas scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns to make it tight, and Josh Allen and the offense did enough to close it out. Dorian Williams picked off a pass for his first career interception along the way.

stories.text: Bye week gives Bills time to mend DJ Moore and others
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore has an AC joint sprain and sat out the last two games. Tight end Dalton Kincaid left Sunday with a rib injury and came back. Bradley Chubb returned from a rib issue but played 21 of 66 snaps, Ed Oliver worked back from a knee problem, and Jordan Hancock is on injured reserve with a calf strain.

stories.text: James Cook delivers the go-ahead score in Las Vegas
stories.summary: Cook carried 22 times for 95 yards and scored the go-ahead touchdown. He added three catches for 58 yards, which made him a factor in both phases of the offense.

stories.text: 258: Josh Allen ties Jim Kelly's franchise touchdown pass mark
stories.summary: Allen threw two touchdown passes against the Raiders, his 258th career total including the playoffs. That ties Kelly for the most in Bills history. He finished 23 of 33 for 255 yards with no interceptions.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Ravens on Nov. 1 without Gardner-Johnson
stories.summary: Buffalo has no game this week. It hosts Baltimore on Nov. 1. The league suspended safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson one game for spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers, so he misses that one and can return Nov. 2. He can appeal.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins stay close but cannot finish

stories.text: Winless Dolphins keep losing close and keep Willis at QB
stories.summary: Miami is 0-5 but has trailed by seven or fewer in the fourth quarter in each of its last three games. Against Cincinnati, the Dolphins cut an 18-point deficit to seven, then missed the extra point and the onside kick. Malik Willis said the team has to get everyone on the same page, and the staff is not considering a switch at quarterback.

stories.text: Seven Dolphins carry questionable tags into Jets game
stories.summary: Caleb Douglas, Reese Taylor, Justin Joly, Robert Beal Jr., JuJu Brents, Michael Taaffe and Jonah Savaiinaea are all listed as questionable for Sunday. Douglas, a rookie receiver, missed the three games before the bye with an ankle injury.

stories.text: Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez leads the NFL in tackles
stories.summary: The second-round pick has 57 tackles through five games, tops in the league. Coach Jeff Hafley praised his communication as the defense's green dot player and said the game is slowing down for him.

stories.text: 2,192: Dolphins rookies lead the league in snaps played
stories.summary: Fourteen rookies have played for Miami through five games, and together they have logged a league-high 2,192 snaps. The running game has benefited too, averaging 5.5 yards per carry since Week 3, third in the NFL.

stories.text: Miami returns from the bye at the Jets on Sunday
stories.summary: The Dolphins visit the 2-4 Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. It starts a stretch of four AFC East games in six weeks. Watch whether the extra week fixes the late-game execution.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots ride a three-game streak to Chicago

stories.text: Patriots beat the Jets 26-19 for a third straight win
stories.summary: New England moved to 4-2 with the win at Gillette Stadium. The Jets cut the lead to one score in the fourth quarter, but the Patriots closed with a field goal drive that ate the clock. Two lost fumbles by Patriots skill players kept the game closer than it needed to be.

stories.text: Vera-Tucker and Brown likely out on the Patriots line
stories.summary: Coach Mike Vrabel said guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and lineman Ben Brown (knee) will probably miss Thursday. Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse would step in. Right tackle Morgan Moses (foot) was limited, and receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited as well.

stories.text: A.J. Brown makes a shaky home debut in New England
stories.summary: Brown played his first home game after missing time since Week 1. He caught three passes for 27 yards, dropped a wide-open deep ball and let a late onside kick bounce off his hands. He remains on the injury report with an ankle issue.

stories.text: 3: Drake Maye strings together three straight 3-TD games
stories.summary: Maye threw three touchdown passes with no interceptions against the Jets. He is the first Patriots quarterback since Tom Brady in 2014 to throw three or more touchdowns in three consecutive games.

stories.text: Patriots visit the Bears on Thursday Night Football
stories.summary: New England (4-2) plays Chicago (4-2) at Soldier Field on Thursday, Oct. 22 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Bears beat Atlanta 31-24 last week with Caleb Williams back from a hamstring injury. Watch the Patriots' patched offensive line against the Bears' pass rush.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets fall to 2-4 and turn to the Dolphins

stories.text: Jets lose to New England and drop to 2-4
stories.summary: The Jets lost 26-19 at Gillette Stadium and now sit third in the AFC East. They also hold three of the top 11 picks in the 2027 draft order, which keeps the quarterback question in view. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. returned and caught passes for more than 100 yards.

stories.text: Breece Hall is questionable after three missed games
stories.summary: Hall has missed three straight games with a quad injury and was inactive against New England. He is listed questionable for Sunday. Receiver Adonai Mitchell is doubtful, and Joseph Ossai, Dylan Parham and Kiko Mauigoa are questionable.

stories.text: Braelon Allen carries the load while Hall sits
stories.summary: Allen ran 17 times for 78 yards and caught two passes for 26 against New England. He leads the Jets with 314 rushing yards on 74 carries and has topped 100 scrimmage yards in two straight games. Coach Aaron Glenn said Allen is showing he can be a bell cow.

stories.text: 3: Jets own three of the top 11 picks in the 2027 draft
stories.summary: New York holds the No. 7 pick from Dallas, the No. 10 pick from Indianapolis and its own No. 11 selection. NFL.com lists quarterback, defensive tackle, cornerback, receiver and linebacker as the biggest needs.

stories.text: Jets host winless Miami on Sunday
stories.summary: New York faces the 0-5 Dolphins at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Miami comes off a bye. Watch whether Hall returns and whether the Jets can hold a lead against a team that has lost close all year.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens blow a lead in Cleveland, face Bengals next

stories.text: Ravens lose 13-10 in Cleveland and share the division lead
stories.summary: Tyler Huntley started again for Baltimore, and the Browns rallied to win on a 37-yard Andre Szmyt field goal on the final snap. The loss ended a three-game Ravens winning streak and left Baltimore and Cleveland tied at 4-2 atop the AFC North. Coach Jesse Minter also criticized kicker Tyler Loop afterward, and the team brought back Jake Moody to the practice squad as competition.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson stays day-to-day with a sprained ankle
stories.summary: Jackson has not played since the Oct. 4 win over Tennessee and could practice this week, per Minter. Center Cam Jurgens is in the concussion protocol and has a real chance to make his Ravens debut. Receiver Rashod Bateman left the Cleveland game with a shoulder injury, but Minter said he should be OK.

stories.text: Trey Hendrickson returns from finger surgery with a sack
stories.summary: The edge rusher came back Sunday with his hand partly wrapped and got to the quarterback in Cleveland. Minter said the team is still monitoring his treatment. His return gives a Ravens defense that held Cleveland scoreless in the first half a boost for the Bengals game.

stories.text: 17: double-digit leads Baltimore has blown since 2018
stories.summary: That total is the most in the NFL over that span, and the Ravens added to it by letting a 10-0 halftime lead slip in Cleveland. Derrick Henry carried 17 times for 58 yards, and the offense could not hold the ball in the second half. The defense wore down late.

stories.text: Bengals visit Baltimore on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati arrives off a bye and with a rested defensive line. Watch whether Jackson returns, who snaps the ball at center, and whether Loop keeps the kicking job. The winner takes sole possession of the early division race.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Rested Bengals head to Baltimore with the division open

stories.text: Bengals return from the bye with the AFC North wide open
stories.summary: The Browns beat the Ravens in Week 6, so every team in the division now has two losses. Cincinnati hits the field rested and heads to Baltimore. The Bengals also made roster moves during the bye, claiming linebacker Jack Kiser on waivers and signing safety Russ Yeast.

stories.text: Dugger back at practice, Howell sidelined by illness
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger returned to practice after missing the Jaguars and Dolphins games. Defensive end Cashius Howell missed practice with an illness, and a couple more missed days would put his Sunday status in doubt. Receiver Colbie Young is working back from a knee injury he suffered in Week 3.

stories.text: Joe Burrow threw four touchdowns in the win at Miami
stories.summary: Burrow went 23 of 32 for 190 yards and four scores in the 31-24 road win over the Dolphins. A week earlier he piled up 428 yards against Jacksonville, with one touchdown and two interceptions, in a 22-17 loss. He now faces a Baltimore defense that held him to a 57.6 percent completion rate across two games last season.

stories.text: 3: of Cincinnati's last four division games are at home
stories.summary: The schedule favors the Bengals down the stretch, and the season ends with Baltimore and Cleveland visiting Paycor Stadium. Dexter Lawrence leads a defensive line that is fully rested for Sunday, though the run defense remains a concern.

stories.text: At Baltimore on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Bengals come off the bye to meet the Ravens. Watch whether Lamar Jackson plays and how Cincinnati handles Derrick Henry. The Bengals then travel to Madrid for Week 9 against Atlanta.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns win another late one and share first place

stories.text: Szmyt kicks Browns past Ravens 13-10 on the final snap
stories.summary: Cleveland trailed 10-0 at the half, then scored 13 straight. Deshaun Watson hit Jerry Jeudy for 33 yards on third down, and Andre Szmyt booted a 37-yard field goal as time expired. Both Cleveland and Baltimore sit at 4-2 atop the AFC North.

stories.text: Delpit in concussion protocol, Jefferson hurt his hip
stories.summary: Safety Grant Delpit left the Ravens game in the first quarter and entered the concussion protocol. Rookie linebacker Justin Jefferson left in the third quarter with a hip injury. Running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and defensive tackle Mason Graham (MCL sprain) sat out Week 6, and receiver Bub Means went to the practice squad injured list with a knee issue.

stories.text: Deshaun Watson goes 14 for 17 in the second half
stories.summary: Watson finished 16 of 26 for 164 yards against Baltimore, and nearly all of that production came after halftime. He accounted for all 13 Cleveland points. Coordinator Todd Monken adjusted to Baltimore's rotating blitzes by attacking the middle of the field.

stories.text: 24: sacks taken by Watson, most in the league
stories.summary: Watson has thrown only two interceptions, but the pocket keeps collapsing. He ties Josh Allen and Bo Nix for the league lead with four fourth-quarter scoring drives. Watson says one of these weeks the offense will click.

stories.text: At Tennessee on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Browns visit Nissan Stadium to face the Titans. Watch the Delpit and Judkins statuses, and whether the offensive line can slow the pressure on Watson. Cleveland plays Pittsburgh in Week 8.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers rally in OT, then fly to Paris

stories.text: Steelers storm back to beat Tampa Bay 26-19 in overtime
stories.summary: Pittsburgh trailed 16-3 after three quarters and scored 13 straight to force overtime. Aaron Rodgers hit rookie Germie Bernard for a 6-yard touchdown in the extra period, and Jalen Ramsey ended the game with a fourth-down sack. The Steelers improved to 4-2.

stories.text: Cornerback Brandin Echols hurt his hamstring on a punt
stories.summary: Echols went down on a first-half punt against Tampa Bay and did not return, and his status is still to be determined. Rookie Daylen Everette is the next option in the secondary. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) missed the past two games, while Michael Pittman Jr. and Derrick Harmon are on injured reserve until Week 10.

stories.text: Aaron Rodgers throws 49 times and wins in overtime
stories.summary: Rodgers went 33 of 49 for 253 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. His fourth-quarter drive started with a third-and-8 throw to DK Metcalf and ended in a short score to Darnell Washington. Bernard and Metcalf each caught 11 passes.

stories.text: 58: yards on Chris Boswell's game-tying field goal
stories.summary: Boswell drilled the long kick to tie the game at 16 and added a 20-yarder to go ahead with 1:21 left in regulation. He missed a 48-yarder wide left in the second quarter. Pittsburgh's 13-point fourth-quarter rally is the franchise's largest since 1992, per CBS Sports.

stories.text: Saints in Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
stories.summary: The Steelers play the Saints at Stade de France in an early-morning kickoff. Watch the Echols situation and how Pittsburgh's pass rush follows up its showing against Tampa Bay. The Steelers host Cleveland in Week 8.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Fairbairn wins it in London, Texans win two straight

stories.text: Fairbairn's buzzer beater lifts Houston in London
stories.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired to beat Jacksonville 34-31 at Wembley. Houston answered a Cam Little 60-yarder that tied the game at 31. The Texans have won two straight after an 0-4 start and sit two games behind the Jaguars in the AFC South.

stories.text: Tank Dell on track for season debut against Giants
stories.summary: Coach DeMeco Ryans said Dell is set to come off injured reserve and play Sunday, with a light snap count. He returned to practice Oct. 7 and took part fully in Week 6 prep. Dell has not played since his Dec. 2024 knee injury.

stories.text: Jaylin Noel tops 100 yards with a touchdown in London
stories.summary: Noel caught for 107 yards and a score against Jacksonville, the best day of his young career for a Houston offense that spread the ball to 10 receivers. Marvin Harrison Jr. added three catches for 34 yards in his Texans debut. Foster Moreau caught two touchdowns.

stories.text: 9:1: C.J. Stroud's touchdown to interception ratio
stories.summary: Stroud threw for 312 yards and three scores against the Jaguars, his third 300-yard game in six weeks. His only interception of the season came in the fourth quarter, when Travis Hunter picked him off in the end zone. Stroud answered with the drive that set up Fairbairn's winner.

stories.text: Giants visit Houston on Sunday at 1:00 ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Texans host New York in Week 7, then take their Week 8 bye. Houston's pass rush has 18 sacks, led by Will Anderson Jr. with 7.5, against a Giants line that has allowed 13. New York has not named a clear starting quarterback.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after 2-4 start

stories.text: Colts fire general manager Chris Ballard
stories.summary: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon let Ballard go Monday, one day after a 26-20 home loss to the previously winless Titans. Assistant GM Ed Dodds will run the personnel department while the team searches for a permanent GM. Ballard finished 72-82-1 in ten seasons, and Indianapolis has not made the playoffs since 2020.

stories.text: Alec Pierce's heel keeps him off the practice field
stories.summary: Coach Shane Steichen said the receiver's 21-day practice window will not open in Week 7. Pierce re-injured his surgically repaired left heel in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City and has finished the required four games on injured reserve. He needs more rehab time first.

stories.text: Daniel Jones stays the starter despite nine turnovers
stories.summary: Steichen said Jones will start against Minnesota. He has turned the ball over nine times, second most in the league behind Justin Herbert. His 59.6 percent completion rate is a career low, and Steichen said Jones knows he has to play better.

stories.text: 8 to 2: Indianapolis giveaways against takeaways
stories.summary: The Colts have committed eight turnovers on offense and forced only two on defense. Jones threw two more interceptions against Tennessee, and Titans special teams blocked a Rigoberto Sanchez punt in the second half. Indianapolis led 13-0 at the break and lost.

stories.text: Colts visit unbeaten Vikings Sunday at 1:00 ET on CBS
stories.summary: Indianapolis faces 5-0 Minnesota in Week 7, then plays at Jacksonville and hosts Dallas. Irsay-Gordon said the firing does not change the team's goals for the season. Watch how Dodds and Steichen handle a locker room that just lost its GM.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars rest on bye after London heartbreaker

stories.text: Jaguars drop a 34-31 decision in London before the bye
stories.summary: Jacksonville lost on Ka'imi Fairbairn's last-second field goal, ending a three-game win streak. The Jaguars stay atop the AFC South at 4-2. Six penalties for 66 yards swung the game by about 14 points, according to the team site.

stories.text: Antonio Johnson hurts ankle in London
stories.summary: Safety Antonio Johnson sustained an ankle injury in the third quarter. Running back Ameer Abdullah cleared a concussion check in the first quarter and returned. The bye gives the team a week to recover, and no official status for Johnson has come out yet.

stories.text: Bhayshul Tuten scores twice as a receiver
stories.summary: Tuten caught four passes for 48 yards and two touchdowns, from 27 and 2 yards, and ran 12 times for 39 yards. Both scores matched his entire 2025 total. He has topped 80 scrimmage yards in four straight games.

stories.text: 426: yards the Jaguars defense allowed to Houston
stories.summary: Houston scored touchdowns on three of four drives from the second quarter through the fourth. Trevor Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns on 24 of 41 passing, and Cam Little's 60-yard field goal tied it at 31. The defense could not get the last stop.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Colts on Nov. 1 at 1:00 ET
stories.summary: Jacksonville is off this weekend. The Jaguars host Indianapolis in Week 8 on CBS. Lawrence carries a 14 to 4 touchdown to interception ratio into the break.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans finally win, rally past Colts 26-20

stories.text: Titans get Saleh his first win with a rally in Indy
stories.summary: Tennessee trailed 13-0 at halftime and beat the Colts 26-20 for its first win of 2026 and Robert Saleh's first as head coach. Joey Slye's 49-yard field goal with 2:03 left won it. The defense sacked the quarterback six times, took the ball away three times and blocked a punt.

stories.text: Alontae Taylor a healthy scratch, status unclear
stories.summary: The cornerback sat out the Colts game and was not on the injury report. Saleh called him a healthy scratch and said the staff will decide what is best for the team. His availability against Cleveland is unannounced.

stories.text: Carnell Tate scores first NFL touchdown
stories.summary: The rookie caught six of seven targets for 70 yards and an 8-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, the team's only offensive score. Over his last four games he has 22 catches for 279 yards. Cam Ward managed just 102 yards passing.

stories.text: 6: sacks by the Titans defense in Indianapolis
stories.summary: Tennessee added three takeaways and a blocked punt, the first team to do all three in a game this season. Jeffery Simmons had two sacks and a forced fumble, and Jermaine Johnson II also had two sacks. Amani Hooker made a career-high 13 tackles.

stories.text: Browns visit Nissan Stadium Sunday at 1:00 ET on CBS
stories.summary: Tennessee hosts Cleveland in Week 7 looking for its first back-to-back wins. Ward has not passed 200 yards in five of six games and sits at 4 touchdowns and 4 interceptions. Watch whether the offense can lean on Tony Pollard, who ran 19 times for 76 yards last week.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos win ugly in OT, sit at 4-2

stories.text: Broncos survive Seattle in overtime, 17-14
stories.summary: Denver held a 14-3 halftime lead, then watched Seattle tie it on a field goal with three seconds left. Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold in overtime, and Denver won it from there. Sean Payton said afterward his team could just as easily be 2-4, and he put the offense's stalled big plays on himself.

stories.text: Moss fought through ribs, Denver thin in secondary
stories.summary: Cornerback Riley Moss practiced on a limited basis with a rib injury before Thursday night and spent much of the game on the sideline. Denver also played without a starting safety, so the Broncos elevated Taylor Rapp and Sean Fresch Jr. from the practice squad. Watch Moss's practice participation this week.

stories.text: McMillian ends it with an overtime pick
stories.summary: McMillian took the ball away from Darnold in overtime and also got credit for a sack. Denver's front also piled up five sacks by the fourth quarter, and Jonah Elliss got his first of the season.

stories.text: 107: Bo Nix's passing yards in the win
stories.summary: Nix finished 17 of 27 for 107 yards with no touchdowns, two sacks and a 71.1 passer rating. The whole Denver offense managed only 168 yards, and the run game and defense carried the night.

stories.text: At Arizona on Sunday, then Chiefs at home
stories.summary: Denver plays the Cardinals on Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on CBS. Payton wants cleaner detail work and more efficient running. The Broncos host Kansas City on Nov. 1 in the next division test.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs stay perfect, trip to Seattle next

stories.text: Chiefs beat Chargers 22-6, stay unbeaten
stories.summary: Kansas City moved to 5-0 and 3-0 in the AFC West, the only undefeated team left in the conference. Patrick Mahomes threw for 272 yards and picked up his 100th regular-season win in his 131st start. The defense sacked Justin Herbert four times.

stories.text: Kelce tweaks ankle, Moore enters concussion protocol
stories.summary: Travis Kelce hurt his right ankle in the first quarter, left several times and came back to finish with four catches for 53 yards. Andy Reid said Kelce might be sore and he is not on the injury list. Jaylon Moore was ruled out with a concussion, and Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Josh Simmons (back) remain out.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker III runs for 128 and two scores
stories.summary: Walker carried 19 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns against the Chargers. His 665 rushing yards lead the NFL. Los Angeles held him to 79 yards on his other 17 carries, but the long runs decided the game.

stories.text: 17 of 44: dropbacks where Chiefs pressured Herbert
stories.summary: Kansas City pressured Justin Herbert on 17 of his 44 dropbacks. George Karlaftis led the way with eight pressures, and the defense finished with four sacks. Nick Bolton added 11 tackles and set the franchise record for 10-tackle games.

stories.text: Chiefs at Seahawks, Sunday night on NBC
stories.summary: Kansas City visits Seattle on Sunday at 8:20 PM ET on NBC at Lumen Field. The Seahawks are 3-3 after their overtime loss in Denver. The Chiefs then visit Denver on Nov. 1.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders fall short to Bills, 3-3 at the break

stories.text: Bills edge Raiders 33-30, ending a three-game streak
stories.summary: Las Vegas dropped back to .500 after Josh Allen and James Cook led Buffalo to the lead for good. Kirk Cousins threw an interception to Dorian Williams that set up a Buffalo touchdown. Coach Klint Kubiak said he was very disappointed and wants his team to close games out.

stories.text: Jeanty's ankle and foot are improving
stories.summary: Ashton Jeanty practiced in a limited role, then sat out, in Week 5 with ankle and foot injuries, and Kubiak said last week he feels much better. Kubiak rejected the idea of resting him. Against Buffalo Jeanty carried 10 times for 22 yards and scored from a yard out.

stories.text: Tre Tucker catches two touchdowns in the loss
stories.summary: Tucker caught five of seven targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns, from 11 and 44 yards out, both from Cousins. He led the team in receiving while Buffalo kept Brock Bowers quiet until the second half. Tucker had two big games in six weeks and fewer than 50 yards in the other four.

stories.text: 378: Raiders yards, 33 more than Buffalo
stories.summary: Las Vegas outgained the Bills 378 to 345 and went 7 of 12 on third down, yet lost by three. The red zone hurt: the Raiders scored touchdowns on two of five trips, while Buffalo hit on three of five.

stories.text: Rams visit Allegiant Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Kubiak spent the week preaching desperation no matter the record. Cousins threw for 313 yards against Buffalo, and the Raiders will need a cleaner red zone to keep up with Matthew Stafford.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers head to the bye with questions

stories.text: Chargers fall to 0-6, Harbaugh to review offense
stories.summary: Kansas City beat Los Angeles 22-6 and stretched the Chargers' losing streak to six. Jim Harbaugh said the offense is not scoring enough and that he will look at everything. The Chargers reached the Chiefs' 1-yard line before a holding penalty forced a field goal.

stories.text: McConkey leaves with concussion before the bye
stories.summary: Ladd McConkey went out in the first quarter with a concussion and did not return. He has 12 catches for 183 yards and a touchdown this season. The bye gives the Chargers time to recover, and one column points to Joe Alt and Tre' Harris as possible returns.

stories.text: Herbert takes a beating behind a hurt line
stories.summary: Justin Herbert took repeated hits against Kansas City and leads the league with eight interceptions, per SportsGrid. Quentin Johnston gave him a 57-yard catch, and a dropped touchdown by Oronde Gadsden cost the offense more.

stories.text: 17 plays, 38 yards: the Chargers' stalled stretch
stories.summary: After four momentum-swinging sequences, the Los Angeles offense ran 17 plays for 38 yards. The Chargers also rank last in the NFL in EPA per play, according to the team's own review of the game.

stories.text: Bye this week, Rams on Nov. 1
stories.summary: The Chargers are off in Week 7. They return Nov. 1 against the Rams at 4:05 PM ET on Fox. Expect questions about play calling and offensive line health in the meantime.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys regroup after second straight loss

stories.text: Cowboys add Pettine, shuffle snaps after Packers loss
stories.summary: Dallas dropped to 2-4 with a 23-13 loss at Green Bay. The coaching staff answered by hiring Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant to help coordinator Christian Parker. The snap counts moved too: Caleb Downs played 40 snaps at slot corner, up from 7 the week before.

stories.text: Turpin and Winters hurt, Durant trending back
stories.summary: KaVontae Turpin has a rib cartilage injury after a hard hit on the opening kickoff, and X-rays came back positive. Linebacker Dee Winters strained his Achilles after recording the team's first interception of the year. Coach Brian Schottenheimer said cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) is trending to play after missing four games.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb climbs the franchise receiving list
stories.summary: Lamb caught 9 passes for 70 yards on 18 targets against Green Bay. That pushed his career total to 7,993 yards and past Tony Hill for third on Dallas's all-time list. The volume was there, but the yards per catch were not.

stories.text: 57-48: Packers out-ran the Cowboys
stories.summary: Green Bay owns the league's worst rushing offense, yet it gained 57 yards on the ground to Dallas's 48. The Cowboys carried 15 times for 48 yards, and Javonte Williams had 41 on 11 carries. Dak Prescott threw 54 times, which Schottenheimer said was not the plan.

stories.text: Monday night in Philadelphia
stories.summary: Dallas visits the 2-4 Eagles on Monday, Oct. 26, at 8:15 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field. Watch whether the run game shows up against an Eagles team starting Tanner McKee at quarterback. Dallas has lost four straight in Philadelphia.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants weigh Winston or McCarthy for Houston

stories.text: Harbaugh closing in on a quarterback call
stories.summary: John Harbaugh said Monday the Giants are honing in on a Week 7 starter at Houston, choosing between Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy replaced Winston with 11:25 left and the Giants down 34-10 to the Saints. Harbaugh noted McCarthy has been in the building only a couple of weeks.

stories.text: Dart, Burns and Adebo remain on injured reserve
stories.summary: The Giants had no practice report posted on Tuesday. Their transaction log lists quarterback Jaxson Dart, outside linebacker Brian Burns and cornerback Paulson Adebo on reserve/injured, along with Chauncey Golston and Braxton Berrios. Dart hurt his knee in Week 2, which put Winston in the lineup.

stories.text: Malik Nabers keeps stacking 100-yard games
stories.summary: Nabers caught 12 passes for 165 yards against New Orleans and earned a Player of the Week nomination. He has 29 catches for 398 yards and two touchdowns over the last three games, topping 100 yards in each. His 168 career receptions rank second through a player's first 25 games.

stories.text: 243: McCarthy's fourth-quarter passing yards
stories.summary: McCarthy threw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter alone against the Saints. That ties the most by a Giant in a single quarter since at least 1991. The Giants still lost 34-27 after committing four turnovers.

stories.text: At Houston, then the bye
stories.summary: The Giants visit the 2-4 Texans on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Houston ranks third in the NFL with 18 sacks, so pocket mobility matters. Both teams are off the following week.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles lose Hurts, and the losses pile up

stories.text: Hurts has clots in his lungs, out for the season
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and clots in both lungs, and he is expected to miss the rest of 2026. The NFL reportedly found the Eagles handled the clearance process appropriately and will not punish them. Tanner McKee is the expected starter.

stories.text: Nine on IR, Barkley still unclear
stories.summary: Philadelphia had nine players on injured reserve as of Tuesday, including Hurts, Tank Bigsby, Grant Calcaterra and Landon Dickerson. Nolan Smith (concussion), Carson Steele (shoulder) and Jordan Davis (ankle) were hurt against Carolina. Saquon Barkley has missed two games with a hamstring strain, and his status for Monday is unclear.

stories.text: Tanner McKee takes over under pressure
stories.summary: McKee went 26 of 45 for 215 yards and one touchdown in the 25-14 loss to Carolina, and the Panthers sacked him three times. He now carries the offense with Hurts on injured reserve. Joe Milton III, who joined from Dallas's practice squad, is the backup.

stories.text: 4: straight losses, the longest of Sirianni's tenure
stories.summary: Philadelphia has lost four in a row, the longest skid in Nick Sirianni's six seasons. The passing offense averages 173.3 yards per game, 26th in the league. DeVonta Smith leads the team with 310 receiving yards.

stories.text: Cowboys visit on Monday night
stories.summary: The Eagles host the 2-4 Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26, at 8:15 p.m. ET at Lincoln Financial Field. Dallas has been outscored 119-67 in its last four games in Philadelphia. Watch Barkley's practice reps and how McKee handles the Dallas pass rush.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: McLaurin out for the year, Commanders on a bye

stories.text: McLaurin tears patellar tendon, done for 2026
stories.summary: Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that captain Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon in the first quarter of the 23-17 loss at San Francisco. He led the team with 230 receiving yards this season. Stefon Diggs, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams absorb the snaps.

stories.text: Mariota, Chenal and Omenihu on the list
stories.summary: Quarterback Marcus Mariota (MCL), linebacker Leo Chenal (neck) and defensive end Charles Omenihu (groin) are all dealing with injuries. Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve with a groin injury. McLaurin is out for the season with the torn tendon.

stories.text: Sonny Styles piles up tackles
stories.summary: The rookie linebacker had 13 tackles and a pass defense against the 49ers. He leads Washington with 46 combined tackles. Styles was the No. 7 overall pick in April.

stories.text: 69: Okonkwo's yards led Washington
stories.summary: Tight end Chig Okonkwo led the Commanders with 69 receiving yards in the loss at San Francisco. McLaurin caught one pass for 27 yards before he left. Okonkwo may see more targets now.

stories.text: Bye week, then Eagles on Sunday night
stories.summary: Washington is off in Week 7. The Commanders return Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC against the Eagles at Northwest Stadium. The bye gives the staff time to rework a receiver group without McLaurin.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams and Gordon return, Pats up Thursday

stories.text: Williams and Gordon return to lift Bears past Atlanta
stories.summary: Caleb Williams came back from a three-game hamstring absence and threw for 305 yards in a 31-23 win over the Falcons. Kyler Gordon made his season debut off the PUP list and piled up three sacks. The Bears are 4-2 and have won three of their last four.

stories.text: Four Bears carry questionable tags into Thursday night
stories.summary: Guard Jonah Jackson, cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, running back Kyle Monangai and linebacker T.J. Edwards are listed as questionable against New England. Jackson left the Atlanta game hurt, and Luke Newman filled in at right guard. Montez Sweat missed the Week 6 game, and Anthony Johnson is on injured reserve.

stories.text: Caleb Williams goes 30 of 36 in his return
stories.summary: Williams threw for 305 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers, good for a 111.2 passer rating. He started 10 of 10 for 122 yards and a score on the first two drives. The Falcons sacked him four times and hit him seven.

stories.text: 3: sacks for Kyler Gordon in his first game back
stories.summary: Gordon added three tackles for loss and a forced fumble to those three sacks. His strip-sack late let Devin Bush recover the ball and seal the win. The Bears sacked Michael Penix Jr. five times as a team.

stories.text: Patriots visit Soldier Field on Thursday night
stories.summary: Chicago hosts New England on Thursday, Oct. 22 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Both teams are 4-2. Watch Williams against Drake Maye, and see how the Bears hold up if Jackson and Stevenson sit.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions come off bye with the Packers next

stories.text: Lions return from bye with a leaky defense and a big stretch
stories.summary: Detroit beat Arizona 45-21 before the bye and now hosts Green Bay and Minnesota in back-to-back games. The offense ties Buffalo for the league lead at 32.8 points per game. The defense is the open question.

stories.text: Branch and Mays near returns for Packers game
stories.summary: Safety Brian Branch, who tore his left Achilles late last season, is close to returning. Center Cade Mays has missed about two months with a wrist injury and is also nearing a comeback. Dan Campbell expects both to play Sunday against Green Bay.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs tops 500 rushing yards with seven scores
stories.summary: Gibbs has run for more than 500 yards and seven touchdowns through five games. Jared Goff has thrown 12 touchdown passes with no interceptions in the same span. The pair drive an offense that Detroit has not slowed once.

stories.text: 404.4: yards per game the Lions defense allows
stories.summary: That is the highest total in the league. Detroit also gives up 29.6 points per game, third worst. The one bright spot is a pass rush with 20 sacks through five games.

stories.text: Packers come to Ford Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Green Bay on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. Minnesota visits the following Sunday. Watch whether Branch and Mays steady a defense that has struggled against the pass.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers on a three-game run, Jacobs returns

stories.text: Josh Jacobs rejoins the Packers after six weeks away
stories.summary: Jacobs spent the first six weeks on the Commissioner's Exempt List after pleading no contest to two misdemeanor battery counts. He returns to practice Wednesday. Matt LaFleur said his status for Sunday at Detroit is still to be determined.

stories.text: Parsons stays out as the defense thins
stories.summary: Micah Parsons remains out, with an eventual return expected. The loss of Edgerrin Cooper hurts the defense going forward. Javon Hargrave did not play against Dallas.

stories.text: Jordan Love throws for 276 yards in Dallas win
stories.summary: Love hit Matthew Golden for a 9-yard touchdown in the 23-13 Sunday night win over the Cowboys. The victory was Green Bay's third straight. The offense got there despite several drops.

stories.text: 22: penalties in a flag-filled game at Lambeau
stories.summary: The Packers and Cowboys combined for 22 flags on Sunday night. Several roughing-the-passer calls drew criticism, including one on Lukas Van Ness that erased a Carrington Valentine interception. Green Bay still pressured Dak Prescott on 37.5 percent of his dropbacks.

stories.text: Division road test at Ford Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Green Bay visits Detroit on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The Lions allow a league-high 404.4 yards per game. Watch whether Jacobs plays and how the Packers run the ball.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings return from bye to host Colts

stories.text: Unbeaten Vikings come off the bye to host Indianapolis
stories.summary: Minnesota is 5-0 and owns the NFL's longest win streak, with a chance to reach 11 straight. Kyler Murray went 24 of 30 for 229 yards in the Week 5 win over New Orleans. The Colts arrive at 2-4.

stories.text: Four offensive starters expected back at practice
stories.summary: Receiver Jordan Addison (hamstring), running back Jordan Mason (thumb, off injured reserve), tackle Christian Darrisaw and tight end T.J. Hockenson (both concussions) are all expected to practice Wednesday. Kevin O'Connell shared the update Tuesday. Josh Oliver and Donovan Jackson are out for the regular season.

stories.text: Aaron Jones piles up 370 yards on 85 carries
stories.summary: Jones has carried 85 times for 370 yards over the past four weeks. He ran for 113 yards at New Orleans in the last game before the bye. He carries the ground game while the receivers heal.

stories.text: 12.8: points per game allowed by the Vikings
stories.summary: Minnesota has given up 64 points through five games. The 1972 Dolphins allowed the same total over the same span. Only the Vikings, Chiefs and 49ers are 5-0.

stories.text: Colts visit U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Indianapolis on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET. Watch how many of the four injured starters play after the bye. Fox Sports also questions the offense, so look for Murray to push the scoring.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons lose another home game, fall to 2-4

stories.text: Falcons dig a 31-7 hole and fall to 0-3 at home
stories.summary: Chicago beat Atlanta 31-23 on Sunday and the Falcons have now lost their first three home games. Michael Penix Jr. took three sacks, two of them strip sacks, and Kyler Gordon's third sack of the day ended the comeback bid with 3:34 left. Coach Kevin Stefanski took responsibility for another slow start.

stories.text: Rookie LB Kendal Daniels leaves on a stretcher with a neck injury
stories.summary: Daniels collided helmet first with Bears tight end Colston Loveland's knee in the third quarter and went to Grady Memorial Hospital. The team said he was conscious and moved all extremities, and he was back at the stadium about two hours later. Stefanski called the early reports good, but no diagnosis or Week 7 status has come out.

stories.text: Zachariah Branch's two fumbles turn into 10 Chicago points
stories.summary: The rookie returner fumbled a punt late in the second quarter and a kickoff late in the third. Chicago turned the first into a touchdown and the second into a field goal that made it 31-7. Special teams has become the clearest fix on Atlanta's list.

stories.text: 154-3: Chicago's first-quarter yardage edge over Atlanta
stories.summary: The Bears outgained the Falcons 154 yards to 3 in the opening 15 minutes and led 14-0 by the end of the quarter. Atlanta outscored Chicago 23-17 the rest of the way, but never recovered from that start.

stories.text: San Francisco visits Atlanta on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Falcons host the 49ers in Week 7, their fourth home game of the season. Atlanta has not beaten San Francisco since 2022 and lost 20-10 last year when Christian McCaffrey piled up more than 200 yards. The Falcons then play at Tampa Bay in Week 8 and have a bye in Week 11.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers beat Eagles, lead the NFC South

stories.text: Panthers beat Eagles 25-14 and hold the NFC South lead
stories.summary: Carolina moved to 3-2 with a road win in Philadelphia, where the Eagles lost their fourth straight. Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards. Tampa Bay comes to Charlotte on Sunday.

stories.text: Jaelan Phillips aggravates his hamstring against Philadelphia
stories.summary: The outside linebacker tweaked the hamstring injury he has been managing, and Thomas Incoom also dealt with a calf injury. Carolina has not given a Week 7 status for either player. Wednesday's practice report will show how much each can do.

stories.text: Bryce Young: 11 touchdowns, two interceptions
stories.summary: Young threw for 281 yards and two scores with no interceptions in Philadelphia. He averages 309.8 passing yards a game this season and has kept the turnovers low. Both touchdowns went to tight end Tommy Tremble, from 12 and 19 yards.

stories.text: 149: penalty yards Carolina gave up and still won by 11
stories.summary: The Panthers drew 13 flags in Philadelphia and still beat the Eagles by 11. Kicker Ryan Fitzgerald hit from 47 and 52 yards, his 11th straight field goal to open the season. Cleaning up the penalties is the obvious fix before a division game.

stories.text: Tampa Bay visits Charlotte on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Carolina hosts the 1-5 Buccaneers at Bank of America Stadium and leads the NFC South at 3-2. The Panthers then travel to Green Bay for a Thursday night game on Prime Video in Week 8. Watch whether Tampa Bay's pass rush, which sacked Aaron Rodgers five times, can reach Young.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints end skid, then fly to Paris

stories.text: Saints run off 34 straight points and beat the Giants 34-27
stories.summary: New Orleans fell behind 10-0 at MetLife Stadium, then snapped a three-game losing streak. Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for another, and the defense forced four turnovers. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. intercepted Jameis Winston, and the Saints stopped the Giants on fourth down at the 12 late.

stories.text: Tyler Shough plays through two broken bones in his left hand
stories.summary: Shough hurt his non-throwing hand on October 5 against Atlanta, and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported two broken bones that will take weeks to heal. He wore a padded glove and handed off with his right hand. The Saints have kept him off the injury report, and he has not missed practice.

stories.text: Alvin Kamara joins a short list with 5,000 and 5,000
stories.summary: Kamara caught a 31-yard touchdown in the third quarter that gave the Saints their first lead. The catch pushed him past 5,000 career receiving yards to go with more than 5,000 rushing yards. He is the sixth player to reach both marks, and Christian McCaffrey is the only other active player on the list.

stories.text: 4: takeaways that carried New Orleans past a bigger yardage total
stories.summary: The Giants outgained the Saints 461 yards to 319, but New Orleans forced four turnovers and lost the ball once. Two of the takeaways were second-half interceptions of Winston, who then gave way to J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Saints face Pittsburgh in Paris on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET
stories.summary: New Orleans plays the Steelers at Stade de France in the first regular-season NFL game in France, with an 8:30 a.m. CT kickoff. The team flew overseas right after the Giants game. The league schedule lists the broadcast on NFL Network, and the Saints are on bye in Week 8.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs blow 16-3 lead, drop to 1-5

stories.text: Bucs lose to Pittsburgh in overtime after leading 16-3
stories.summary: Tampa Bay led by 13 entering the fourth quarter, then Pittsburgh scored on five straight possessions and won 26-19 in overtime. Germie Bernard caught the winning 6-yard touchdown, and Jalen Ramsey sealed it with a fourth-down sack. The Bucs are 1-5 and trail Carolina in the division.

stories.text: Baker Mayfield expected to practice Wednesday after three missed games
stories.summary: Mayfield dislocated his throwing thumb late in Week 3 against Minnesota and has not practiced since. Coach Todd Bowles said he is supposed to work Wednesday and must show he can grip and throw at full velocity. If he cannot, rookie Jalon Daniels makes a fourth straight start.

stories.text: Jalon Daniels: 501 yards, 3 TDs and 5 INTs in the Bucs' 1-2 stretch
stories.summary: The rookie quarterback has completed 60 of 98 passes and run 20 times for 126 yards. He threw two interceptions against Pittsburgh as Tampa Bay lost its fourth quarter lead. Tampa Bay is 1-2 in his starts.

stories.text: 5: sacks of Aaron Rodgers, a season high for Tampa Bay
stories.summary: The Bucs rushed well enough to sack Rodgers five times, two by outside linebacker David Walker. Cornerback Keionte Scott added a sack and eight tackles, and A'Shawn Robinson intercepted a pass. The defense still gave up a 253-yard passing day.

stories.text: Bucs visit Carolina on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Tampa Bay travels to Bank of America Stadium to face the 3-2 Panthers, who lead the NFC South. Bowles called the game critical, and a win would even the all-time series at 26-26. Atlanta visits Tampa Bay in Week 8.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: LaFleur beats McVay on a last-second kick

stories.text: LaFleur tops his old boss as Ryland kicks Arizona past L.A.
stories.summary: Chad Ryland hit a 43-yard field goal as time expired, and the Cardinals beat the Rams 18-16 as double-digit underdogs. Mike LaFleur, in his first year as head coach, won his first meeting with former boss Sean McVay. Arizona's second win of the season came without a touchdown.

stories.text: Nolen hurts ankle, Love sits and stays questionable
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Walter Nolen III hurt his ankle in the second half against the Rams. Running back Jeremiyah Love missed that game with an ankle injury and carries a questionable tag into Week 7, along with Andrew Wingard and Wydett Williams Jr. James Conner and Paris Johnson are on injured reserve.

stories.text: Ryland kicks six field goals, the last one wins it
stories.summary: Chad Ryland accounted for all 18 Arizona points with six field goals, the last from 43 yards on the final snap. Jacoby Brissett supported him with 218 passing yards.

stories.text: 16: Wins McVay had in 19 meetings with Arizona before Sunday
stories.summary: Sean McVay had beaten the Cardinals 16 times in 19 tries before LaFleur broke the pattern. The Arizona defense held the NFL's top total offense to 286 yards, a sharp turn for a unit that ranked among the league's worst earlier this season.

stories.text: Broncos visit State Farm Stadium Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Arizona hosts Denver on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Brissett starts, and the defense ranks 28th in yards per play allowed, so watch whether Sunday's showing against the Rams holds up.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams lose again and the injuries pile up

stories.text: McVay says Rams are beating themselves in a 2-4 start
stories.summary: The Rams fell 18-16 at home to the Cardinals, their third loss in four games. McVay pointed to the unforced errors, mostly on offense, as the reason his team keeps losing. Matthew Stafford lost a ball on a strip sack during a first-half two-point try, and Tyler Higbee fumbled midway through the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Adams out 6 to 10 weeks, Grupe and Ford done for the year
stories.summary: Davante Adams ruptured a hamstring tendon and should miss six to ten weeks. Kicker Blake Grupe (torn ACL) and nose tackle Poona Ford (ruptured triceps) are out for the season. Kobie Turner has a groin strain and likely heads to IR, while Trent McDuffie's groin status for Las Vegas gets decided at the end of the week.

stories.text: Stafford throws for two scores, but the offense stalls late
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns against Arizona. Puka Nacua caught six passes, three on the final drive, which ended on downs. Colby Parkinson's late touchdown stood only after video review.

stories.text: 286: Yards for the NFL's top offense against Arizona
stories.summary: Los Angeles came in leading the league in total offense and managed 286 yards. The Rams turned the ball over twice in Arizona territory in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Rams head to Las Vegas for their first Allegiant visit
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at the Raiders on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. It is the Rams' first game at Allegiant Stadium, and they have won the last two meetings. Watch who kicks, and whether McDuffie is back.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers hold off Washington to stay unbeaten

stories.text: 49ers survive a Commanders rally to reach 6-0
stories.summary: San Francisco led by 20 and held on for a 23-17 win on Monday night. Jayden Daniels threw two second-half touchdowns to close the gap. Malik Mustapha broke up a fourth-down pass at the goal line with 1:54 left, and Keion White and Ogbo Okoronkwo sacked Daniels on the last play.

stories.text: Evans' Achilles tendinitis flares, Deebo out past the bye
stories.summary: Mike Evans left the Commanders game with Achilles tendinitis, and Kyle Shanahan said it is not believed to be long term. Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Demarcus Robinson are not expected back until after the Week 8 bye. Christian Kirk had two strong practices after a calf injury and is a Week 7 option.

stories.text: McCaffrey scores twice on the ground in Santa Clara
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey ran for two touchdowns against Washington, including a 1-yard score in the first quarter. Brock Purdy added 264 passing yards and an 11-yard touchdown to George Kittle. The early lead proved large enough to survive the Commanders' comeback.

stories.text: 105.6: Purdy's career passer rating, the best in NFL history
stories.summary: After crossing the 1,500-attempt threshold, Brock Purdy's 105.6 rating sits above Lamar Jackson's 102.7 for the top career mark. Purdy went 21 of 29 for 264 yards on Monday.

stories.text: Unbeaten Niners travel to Atlanta before the bye
stories.summary: San Francisco visits the Falcons on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX, then has a bye in Week 8. Watch the Evans and Kirk status at receiver.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks stew over a second straight loss

stories.text: Seattle drops 17-14 in overtime despite outgaining Denver
stories.summary: The Seahawks lost to the Broncos on Thursday night when Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal in overtime. Seattle fell to 3-3, its second loss in five days. Mike Macdonald said afterward his team lacked its identity and promised cleaner football.

stories.text: Charbonnet and Bradford near returns, Arroyo likely to IR
stories.summary: Running back Zach Charbonnet has a good chance to play Sunday after his torn ACL from January, and guard Anthony Bradford returned to practice Monday after a month on IR. Tight end Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) is out a significant time and most likely headed to IR. Rookie back Jadarian Price (chest) cannot return before Sunday.

stories.text: Darnold takes the heat after a 51-throw night
stories.summary: Sam Darnold went 27 of 51 for 278 yards with two interceptions against Denver, the second on the Broncos' first overtime possession. The yardage is his second-highest of the season, but he has seven interceptions on the year. He was also sacked five times and hit 17.

stories.text: 353: Seattle's yards against a Denver offense held to 168
stories.summary: Seattle outgained Denver 353 to 168 and had 24 first downs to the Broncos' 13, and still lost. Two late Darnold interceptions and an earlier fumble erased that edge.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Seattle on Sunday night
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Kansas City on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Seahawks need a clean game from the quarterback and a healthier backfield.
